title: Old, stopped: quadratic reciprocity, first try at fair prompts. Duplicates wasted shared and OSO turns; replaced by the current run (Nov 27)
question: With the same prompt size in every setup (the newest 60 lemmas shown, the rest found by search), does OSO get further into quadratic reciprocity than working alone or a shared library, for the same $4 a run? Repeats qr-1-long, whose shared setups paid about twice as much a turn to read the whole library. One run each: a first look. [A]
answer: Stopped early, not a fair comparison. Only the newest 60 lemmas were shown, so shared and OSO labs often re-proved lemmas already in the library; Lean refused each as a duplicate and the turn ended. That wasted about a quarter of their turns (94 and 104 of about 390), against 18 of 363 for working alone. Replaced by qr-3, where a duplicate tells the lab the name and lets it try again, and half the lemmas shown are those related to its recent tries.

targets.text: Quadratic reciprocity, from scratch: for two different odd primes p and q, q is a square remainder mod p exactly when p is one mod q, unless both p and q leave remainder 3 when divided by 4; then exactly one of them is.
targets.statement: : ∀ p q : N, Prime p → Prime q → p ≠ q → two < p → two < q → ((IsSq p q ↔ IsSq q p) ↔ (ModEq (two * two) p 1 ∨ ModEq (two * two) q 1))

areas: Numbers from scratch (deep set): addition, multiplication, order, divisibility, primes, binomial coefficients and congruences, built from zero and successor.
Quadratic reciprocity (QR set): remainders, products over a range, counting, and squares mod a prime, on the same numbers built from zero and successor.
